summary: Investigated why a clicked 'Install' of the codex extension did not appear in the Gizmo UI. Confirmed the install itself succeeded (manifest, Pi junction, and web bundle symlink all present), but Gizmo's agent-server loads its extension catalog once at process startup via registerExtensions (apps/agent-server/src/server.ts:40) with no rescan on link, so the running server's in-memory catalog still omitted codex. Restarted the managed dev server (pnpm dev:server:restart, PID 28852 -> 24152) so the new catalog is picked up; user is told to refresh the browser so installWebExtensions runs again on reconnect.
decisions: Treated the install click as having succeeded; root cause is the agent-server's one-shot startup catalog scan, not the install flow itself.
Restarted the managed dev server via pnpm dev:server:restart (rather than asking the user to do it) because the restart is needed for the new linked extension to appear in the in-memory catalog.
Recommended a browser refresh after restart because ConnectionCapability.installWebExtensions runs on websocket reconnect to fetch and register web bundles (including codex.web.js).
Flagged as a Gizmo UX gap that linking an extension while the server is running requires a server restart with no UI hint; suggested a follow-up to make registryLink trigger a server-side rescan.
errors: Symptom reported: clicking Install in the Gizmo extension UI did not cause the codex extension to show up. Cause: agent-server's registerExtensions call runs once at process start (apps/agent-server/src/server.ts:40), so extensions linked after startup are missing from registeredExtensions() -> ProjectIntegrationResolver output -> enabledExtensionIds, hiding status bar item and inspector tab.

Pre-existing, unrelated client-side noise in .gizmo-dev/dev-server.log: marked renderer.link errors from marked@18.0.9 and ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications errors from @vite/client; not caused by and not blocking the install.
